summary: Resolved the OWNER_DECISION_REQUIRED ambiguity in the T069 acceptance clause by adopting Reading (b): one RunRequest carries exactly one pool_key_id and publishes exactly one manifest under the request's own run_id; multi-pool coverage is achieved through separate RunRequests whose manifests share dataset_version, reporting_numeraire and valuation_qualification under their respective run_ids. Removed the 'one manifest per member pool under one run identity' phrasing and rewrote the acceptance clause to match the deliverables' singular 'the pool and block range' wording. No other contract fields, dependencies, or workflow state changed.
rationale: The triage-002 report identified a single ambiguity in the T069 acceptance clause: 'one manifest per member pool under one run identity' could be read as (a) one RunRequest naming multiple pools with one manifest per pool under a single run_id, or (b) one RunRequest per pool, each publishing one manifest under its own run_id, with manifests sharing dataset_version, reporting_numeraire and valuation_qualification. The Owner recorded Reading (b) as the correct product intent. The current implementation (RunRequest declares a single pool_key_id; submit publishes one manifest per request; _MANIFEST_FILENAME is keyed per (run_id, pool_key_id); test_two_heterogeneous_pools_share_run_identity issues two separate RunRequests and asserts the shared fields under their respective identities) matches Reading (b). The deliverables' phrasing 'the pool and block range' is singular, which is consistent with Reading (b). The acceptance clause was the only place where 'member pool(s)' and 'one run identity' met. The new acceptance clause: (1) opens with the deliverables' wording 'a new run request naming the dataset version, the registered strategy identity and its parameters, the pool and block range, and the seed, fill, cost and quote assumptions'; (2) makes Reading (b) explicit by stating one RunRequest carries exactly one pool_key_id and publishes exactly one manifest under the request's own run_id; (3) retains the two-heterogeneous-pool-fixtures scenario but reframes it as two separate RunRequests sharing dataset_version, reporting_numeraire and valuation_qualification under their respective run_ids; (4) removes the 'one manifest per member pool under one run identity' phrasing entirely. The remaining acceptance bullets (byte-equivalent rerun, product rerun source-preservation, cancellation/failure closed, in-flight restart, fail-closed validation, offline CLI) are unchanged. No dependency, workflow state, attempt, evidence, commit SHA, runtime model, or approval data was touched.
